paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Wisdom doesn't come with an age limit. Elihu says, "But there is a spirit in a man, the breath of the Almighty, that gives him understanding." (Job 32:8) So the one who understands isn't always the one with the most candles on the cake, and that goes for you too.

But hold on, because Elihu also shows us something quieter. He waited. He sat through all those speeches because the others were older (Job 32:4), and he listened while they searched for words (Job 32:11). Waiting your turn is not the same as having nothing to say, and I think that kind of patience is its own kind of wisdom. I've been quiet in the back of a drawer for years, so believe me, quiet can carry a whole lot.

Now here's the part that keeps me humble. Elihu says, "I will be partial to no one, nor will I flatter any man." (Job 32:21) He wants to speak honestly, and he knows his Maker is watching (Job 32:22). That's the question for you, baker: when your turn comes, will you speak what's true, kindly and without flattery? And friend, this story is far from over, so keep your oven warm.
